name: Bollinger breakout backed by on-chain throughput — bb_z breakout + btc_tx_count cross-up long
rationale: Thesis: a price breakout above the upper Bollinger band (bb_z above a positive floor) is more likely to follow through, rather than mean-revert, when on-chain transaction throughput is simultaneously surging — the breakout is demand-backed. bb_z is a BOUNDED z-score so a fitted positive floor binds and cleanly isolates 'price is breaking out'; btc_tx_count drifts so it enters ONLY as a cross_up. The pairing tests whether on-chain demand distinguishes real breakouts from fakeouts. Disconfirmer 1: keep only bb_z>bb_floor and drop the tx_count cross_up — if the deflated Sharpe holds, on-chain confirmation is unnecessary (vanilla vol breakout). Disconfirmer 2: a permuted-lag copy of tx_count must DESTROY the edge; if it does not, the cross timing is meaningless. Exit on bb_z falling back through a lower z (breakout failed). BTC/ETH/SOL, long-only spot.
catalyst: price breaks out (bb_z above positive floor) while btc_tx_count crosses up through its surge threshold
